title: Building LLM Features: Structured Output, Tool Calling & Streaming
concept: Ship LLM features in JavaScript that survive production: prompts as versioned contracts, structured output validated before use, retry and repair with a limit, safe tool calling, streaming that survives a cut connection, timeouts and fallbacks, per-user token budgets and tests with a fake model, so every challenge is deterministic.
description: An intermediate course for developers who build product features on top of an LLM API. The whole course builds one real feature - the CodeDev Hint Service, which reads a learner's failing code and returns a three-level hint - and every lesson starts from something that went wrong with it: a hint that broke the page because the model returned prose instead of JSON, a retry loop that turned one bad answer into fifty calls, a tool call with arguments nobody checked, a stream cut in the middle of a word, a bill that grew eight times in two days, a hint that pasted the reference solution. You fix each one with code you can test: versioned prompt templates, schema validation, bounded retry and repair, argument validation for tools, stream assembly, timeouts and static fallbacks, token quotas, and fake LLMs with recorded fixtures. 11 lessons with quizzes on real logs and JavaScript challenges, including "Spot the AI Mistake" fixes. No real model is called.
